> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/insert-interval)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

You are given a collection of closed intervals `intervals` that are pairwise disjoint and sorted by their start times, and an additional interval `newInterval`. Insert `newInterval` into the list. If `newInterval` overlaps with any existing interval (treating touching endpoints as overlap), merge them into a single interval. Return the resulting collection of intervals, still sorted by start value and with no overlaps.

Implement a one-pass algorithm that runs in $$O(n)$$ time and uses only $$O(1)$$ extra space besides the output list.

Example 1:

```text
Input: intervals = [[1,4],[6,8],[10,12]], newInterval = [4,9]
Output: [[1,9],[10,12]]
```

Explanation: `newInterval` starts at 4, which touches `[1,4]` and also covers `[6,8]`; all three merge into `[1,9]`. The suffix `[10,12]` remains unchanged.

Example 2:

```text
Input: intervals = [[2,3],[5,7],[8,9]], newInterval = [1,2]
Output: [[1,3],[5,7],[8,9]]
```

Explanation: `[1,2]` shares the endpoint 2 with `[2,3]`, so they merge into `[1,3]`. The rest are untouched because their start points are greater than 3.

Example 3:

```text
Input: intervals = [], newInterval = [4,7]
Output: [[4,7]]
```

Constraints:

* $$0 \le \text{intervals.length} \le 1000$$
* $$\text{intervals[i].length} == 2$$
* $$0 \le \text{start}_i \le \text{end}_i \le 5000$$
* `intervals` is ordered by $$\text{start}_i$$ and contains no overlapping intervals.
* $$\text{newInterval.length} == 2$$
* $$0 \le \text{start} \le \text{end} \le 5000$$

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

The intervals are already sorted and disjoint, so you can scan linearly and decide where the new interval fits.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

There are three cases: the new interval lies completely before all others, overlaps some, or lies completely after, handle them in a single pass.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

When merging overlapping intervals, keep updating the start and end of the new interval and skip merged ones, be careful about touching endpoints (treat as overlap).

</details>
